{{Short description|German inventor and scientist}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=September 2023}}
'''Gerhard M. Sessler''' (born 15 February 1931 in Rosenfeld, [[Baden-Württemberg]], Germany)<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ea.tu-darmstadt.de/elektroakustik_nt/personal_ea_nt/detail_mitarbeiter_ea_nt_2_22656.en.jsp|title=Gerhard M. Sessler|last=Elektroakustik|first=Fachgebiet|website=Fachgebiet Elektroakustik – Technische Universität Darmstadt|language=en|access-date=1 November 2019|archive-date=1 November 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191101211153/https://www.ea.tu-darmstadt.de/elektroakustik_nt/personal_ea_nt/detail_mitarbeiter_ea_nt_2_22656.en.jsp|url-status=dead}}</ref> is a German inventor and scientist. He is [[Emeritus|Professor emeritus]] at the [[Department of Electrical Engineering and Information Technology of TU Darmstadt|Department of Electrical Engineering and Information Technology]] of the [[Technische Universität Darmstadt]].

Together with [[James West (inventor)|James E. West]], he invented the [[foil electret microphone]]<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Sessler | first1 = G. M. | last2 = West | first2 = J. E. | year = 1962 | title = Self-biased condenser microphone with high capacitance | journal = Journal of the Acoustical Society of America | volume = 34 | issue = 11| pages = 1787–1788 | doi=10.1121/1.1909130| bibcode = 1962ASAJ...34.1787S }}</ref> at [[Bell Laboratories]] in 1962. Together with [[Dietmar Hohm]], he invented the [[MEMS microphone]], also known as the [[silicon microphone]] in 1983.<ref name="Darmstadt" /><ref>{{cite web | last=Nass | first=Richard | title=Pioneers of MEMS mikes keep the faith | website=Embedded | url=https://www.embedded.com/pioneers-of-mems-mikes-keep-the-faith/}}</ref>

== Life ==
[[Image:US Patent 3118022 - Gerhard M. Sessler James E. West - Bell labs - electroacustic transducer - foil electret condenser microphone 1962 1964 - pages 1-3.png|thumb|280x140px|right|First patent on foil electret microphone by G. M. Sessler and J. E. West (pages 1 to 3)]]

From 1950 to 1959, Sessler studied physics at Universities of [[University of Freiburg|Freiburg]], Munich, and [[University of Göttingen|Göttingen]]. He received his [[diplom]]a in 1957 and his Ph.D. from the [[University of Göttingen]] in 1959. After working in the United States at [[Bell Labs]] until 1975, he returned to the academia in Germany. From 1975 to 2000, he worked as a professor of [[electrical engineering]] at the [[Department of Electrical Engineering and Information Technology of TU Darmstadt|Department of Electrical Engineering and Information Technology]] of the [[Darmstadt University of Technology|Technische Universität Darmstadt]] where he invented the silicon microphone.<ref name="Darmstadt">{{Cite web|url=https://www.tu-darmstadt.de/universitaet/mitten_in_der_gesellschaft/geschichte_persoenlichkeiten/persoenlichkeiten_1/gerhard_m_sessler/index.de.jsp|title=Gerhard M. Sessler|last=Darmstadt|first=Technische Universität|website=Technische Universität Darmstadt|language=de|access-date=1 November 2019}}</ref> In 1999, Sessler was named [[Professor emeritus]] at the same university.

He holds over 100 international [[patents]], among them 18 US-patents. The first one, US 3,118,022, with James E. West, was issued on 14 January 1964.<ref>{{Cite patent|title=Electroacoustic transducer|gdate=1962-05-22|url=https://patents.google.com/patent/US3118022A/en}}</ref>

Sessler is the author/editor of several books on [[Electret|electrets]] and [[acoustics]]. In 2014, together with [[Ning Xiang]], he co-edited a memorial book on [[Manfred R. Schroeder]] published by Springer.<ref>Ning Xiang and Gerhard M. Sessler: Acoustics, Information, and Communication – Memorial Volume in Honor of Manfred R. Schroeder{{cite book|title=Acoustics, Information, and Communication – Memorial Volume in Honor of Manfred R. Schroeder, Springer 2014|doi=10.1007/978-3-319-05660-9|chapter=Acoustics, Information, and Communication|year=2015|isbn=978-3-319-05659-3|editor1-last=Xiang|editor1-first=Ning|editor2-first=Gerhard M|editor2-last=Sessler}}</ref> Furthermore, he is well known for his over 300 scientific papers in prestigious international magazines and journals.

Gerhard Sessler was married to Renate Sessler (now deceased) and has three children: Cornelia, Christine and Gunther.
